g.text: colour = % of substrates with a residue of that class at that position · rows alphabetical · the six classes partition the 20 residues, so every column sums to 100%

text.style: font-size: 5.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #666666

g.text: Colour and cell text are the same number: the percentage of the n = 20 P/G-D/E/T substrates with that class at that position (one peptide = 5%). Blank = 0%, no peptide in the group.

text.style: font-size: 5.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #666666

g.text: Rows are alphabetical; the chip beside each label is its chemical class.

text.style: font-size: 5.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #666666

g.text: This is composition, NOT enrichment — a residue frequent here may be just as frequent among the controls. * above a cell = it also differs between the two groups at Fisher exact p <

text.style: font-size: 5.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #666666

g.text: 0.05 (4 of 126 testable class cells, against 6 expected by chance alone; 1 survives FDR correction). Compare with Figure 18b / 19b for positions 4–12 for the other group, and with

g.text: This panel is the N-terminal window only — positions 4–12, out to the 12th amino acid of the 24-mer — on the same 0–45% scale as the full 4–24 version, so the two are read the same way.
